notes: Spec asserts: ready → working → ready with at least one tool call mid-turn, and state NEVER enters waiting. The recipe drives one auto-executed bash call ('echo hello') followed by a terminal 'done' reply. Copilot is launched with --allow-all, so no permission.requested is written and `waiting` — reachable ONLY via the parser's permission_requested event — is structurally unreachable; the tool.execution_start/complete pair is continued working activity and assistant.turn_end is the only ready settle. If a recording ever flips to waiting here, the bash call tripped a gate (the sibling gated-tool scenario) and the launch flags must be tightened, not this spec. PRESESSION BIRTH: copilot creates its session-state directory at launch but writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so processlifecycle emits a transient proc-<PID> row first (scanner.go:347) and the real dir-keyed session id arrives later — modelled as two phases with every later phase anchored same_session_as session_birth, templated from the mistral-vibe sibling. The phase DSL has no tool-event form, so the auto-executed call is asserted through the single uninterrupted working span it sustains plus the no-waiting invariant. OBSERVATIONS: cost/tokens are asserted non-zero and ARE derivable from the staged transcript offline (assistant.message.outputTokens is Copilot's live token signal; gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4-5 are both priced in the committed replay capacity snapshot). model is deliberately unpinned — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, both observed in one live 1.0.77 session; record fills it from the recording.
